value: Kuro was 16 years 7 months old. He had lived with an inoperable splenic mass since Jun-Jul 2024, managed with palliative care (prednisolone, darbepoetin, iron, acupuncture), along with arthritis, progressive hind-limb weakness and cataracts. At his last FurKids check-up on 14 Sep 2026 his weight had gone up to 19.7 kg. His blood work showed mild anaemia (HCT 34.9%) and a high urea (13.0 mmol/L), with normal creatinine, liver and pancreatic values, and a negative tick-borne and heartworm test. He was given antibiotics for an inflamed leg wound, an injection, and parasite treatment. At acupuncture on 1-2 Oct his carer reported "hind legs weak but overall okay", with his heart and lungs sounding good. His acupuncture vet found him "clear" apart from progressive hind-limb weakness, with "crampy" hind-limb and spine muscles. She recommended home massage and told us to "continue making his life heaven on earth". In his last two weeks he had mostly good days: on 8 Oct his acupuncture vet said he was doing much better, and on the day he died he was energetic, looking for titbits near the terrace. He slipped into a small open fish pond about 5 feet from his dad, without a sound; no one saw him go in, and he was found about 2.5 hours later. The post mortem found a large splenic tumour with a partial, not-fresh rupture and lung congestion, and could not determine whether he collapsed before entering the water. I believe the most likely explanation is a sudden deterioration, possibly related to the tumour, on a background of old age and weak hind legs.
